answer: Latent Coordination Clustering. Each identity's actions emit a behavioral trace; after the fact, a raven pass clusters traces by shared timing and phrasing signatures. Any cluster above a size threshold has its members flagged, and their downstream gains are clawed back. To evade, an attacker must vary behavior enough to bridge unrelated clusters, forcing costly per-identity distinctness: unique pacing, vocabulary, and schedules. A detectable plume of correlated activity still remains, so marginal identities must be run at near-human overhead.
